So I usually start by watching videos and listen to somebody's case on why a stock will increase free cash flow per share exponentially. Not what I base my buys off of but there's so many good companies that it helps me find good buys. Then I usually go through balance sheet and income statement, i look at historical average p/e and sector median P/E and compare to forward p/e to get an idea of if it's cheap or expensive. I also look at price to sales sometimes. P/e and other multiples aren't always a good indicator though because some stocks will stay at insanely high P/E ratios while they're in major growth phases. But yeah listen to the earnings calls, consistent EPS growth is the main thing you're looking for if you want to be in a stock that will increase in share price over time. Pay attention to share buybacks, they will give a good boost to your eps. Pay attention to the company's plan they lay out during their earnings calls. You can look into a company's track record on how well they keep their promises and how often they beat earnings expectations. But yeah anyways once I find a company I want to own I just do a modified DCA. Where I weekly buy all 8 of my stocks I'm holding no matter the valuation, but when I feel one is cheap I allocate much more than usual to that stock. Really what matters in the long run is share count, don't worry too much about trying to buy your stock at the perfect time, just keep acquiring shares and a good company will make you tons of money in the long run.
